project.name: ccp
project.description: AI-native compliance automation platform (teaching-scale reference build). Connectors land immutable evidence from GitHub, HRIS, Okta, AWS and manual uploads, and uploads get admissibility and adequacy feedback within seconds; normalization and identity resolution build canonical people, access grants, assets and evidence; a SOC 2 / ISO 27001 knowledge catalogue maps controls to tests that tiered evaluators decide with verified citations into a bitemporal compliance state, while AWS coverage is measured from the account's own inventory. After a FAIL, CCP looks up what changed, writes or lets the Investigator choose a catalogue fix that code renders and checks, and suggests it: a person applies it and only a later read confirms it. Read-only agents investigate, draft policy, answer questions and run long audit tasks; security questionnaires are answered by a fixed pipeline; one human approval stage, with measured autonomy for low-impact drafts, gates every decision; and eval gates, published quality snapshots, replay, a signed audit chain and offline-verifiable audit packages make the records trustworthy.

nodes.name: Evidence Ingestion
nodes.summary: Collects compliance evidence from GitHub, HRIS (fixture or Merge aggregator), Okta, AWS and manual upload folders. Every pull is a recorded sync run with per-scope outcomes, and every provider event or response is landed once into an immutable raw zone (local or S3 Object Lock) and announced on the event log; lookups, inventory snapshots and playbook reads land their responses here too.

businessRules: The raw zone is write-once: repeats are diverted under dups/ and S3 objects use Object Lock
Event ids are derived from content, so an unchanged re-pull lands no duplicates
A content-addressed event that repeats an earlier state lands again as a re-observation once its stream has moved on, so a returning state is never hidden
A scope never reached counts as failed; a listing the credential cannot see is a gap, never an empty listing
Requests spend tokens from a per-(tenant, connection) rate bucket and follow a per-endpoint error table
Manual uploads take the tenant only from the folder, require a manifest and extract PDFs in a capped subprocess
An AWS role is used only after verification proves it needs CCP's external ID and cannot write
crossDomainInteractions: Appends raw.<connector> records to the event log for normalization
Lands the raw responses of lookups, inventory snapshots and playbook reads before anything is recorded about them
Re-pulled by the opt-in live GitHub removal to re-evaluate after a change
Raw objects are re-hashed by the audit integrity checks and pointed to from audit packages

nodes.name: Event Processing & Scheduling
nodes.summary: A Postgres event_log used as a Kafka-style queue with ordered and parallel topics, leased claims, retries, parking and dead letters. A fair multi-tenant dispatcher serves each consumer across tenants, and per-tenant wall-clock schedules fire jobs exactly once.

businessRules: Ordered topics are processed per tenant in (source_ts, seq) order under an advisory lock
Parallel claims are leased and every status change is fenced on the lease token
Retryable errors back off, throttling does not spend an attempt, terminal errors dead-letter at once, an exhausted budget parks the record
The tenant served longest ago is claimed first so no tenant starves
Each schedule slot fires once across processes and every job is safe to run twice
crossDomainInteractions: Carries evaluations, verdicts, lookups, investigations, fix confirmations, evidence feedback, adequacy, applies and task_items work for the other domains
Fires clock, full-run, sync, connection-check, sentinel, audit-checkpoint, transcription, inventory, registry-diff, playbook, answer-staleness and autonomy-watch jobs

nodes.name: Entity Normalization & Identity Resolution
nodes.summary: Turns raw provider events into canonical, append-only entity observations (persons, access grants, assets, evidence, vendors) through pure mappers, then resolves which accounts across systems belong to the same person. Uncertain matches go to a human through the approval stage.

businessRules: Mappers are pure and entity inserts are idempotent observations
A null, empty or unknown value never overrides a known one when person observations merge
Grant revocations are derived only from a listing seen whole
Pairs mixing a human with a service or shared account are gated out before scoring
An unknown account kind is never auto-merged; every decision is logged
Entities under an open review make dependent tests report needs_review
crossDomainInteractions: Announces every new entity on the entities topic, which drives the impact step and upload feedback
Supplies canonical links and pending reviews to the evaluation context
Routes identity merges through the human approval stage

nodes.name: Evidence Retrieval & Indexing
nodes.summary: Chunks current, admissible evidence page by page, optionally enriches chunks with context, embeds them through a cache into versioned index generations, and serves hybrid full-text plus pgvector search with reranking. Calibration against distractors and per-type gates decide when a new embedder may serve.

businessRules: Chunk ids are content-addressed over tenant, evidence, page, ordinal, text and chunker version
A model-transcribed upload with a blocking admissibility reason is left out of the index
Generations and activations are insert-only; a candidate serves only after the retrieval gate passes
Retrieval refuses chunks embedded with a different model than the query embedder
An unreachable embedder degrades search to the lexical arm; an unreachable reranker keeps fused order
Text is redacted before any embedding or rerank provider sees it, and Voyage needs the recorded training opt-out
crossDomainInteractions: Feeds tier 2 and tier 3 evaluators, questionnaire answers and agent tools with cited evidence chunks
Provides calibrated retrieval confidence to the confidence score

nodes.name: Evidence Admissibility & Adequacy
nodes.summary: Gives an uploader feedback seconds after a document lands: every document version is segmented deterministically into citable headings, sentences and table cells, code applies per-type admissibility rules and a provenance badge, and an adequacy verifier asks whether an auditor would accept the document, held in shadow until it agrees with auditors' own accept-or-flag labels.

businessRules: Segment ids are stable per document version; a model cites ids and code renders the quote, returning unknown ids instead of rendering them

Admissibility is code: no issue date, a future date, a document too old for its type, a missing or inverted period, a screenshot offered for a period, an unresolved subject or a visible date far from the stated one blocks
Segments and code feedback are given once per document version, with no model call
The adequacy verifier sees the document only as fenced, numbered segments and cites segment ids, never quotes
An accept that cites no segment showing the control is turned into a flag, since accepting what an auditor would flag is the costly error
Live mode is downgraded to shadow until calibration against auditor labels passes, including a Clopper-Pearson upper bound on false accepts
Adequacy jobs park while no model key is available
crossDomainInteractions: Consumes new evidence versions from the entities topic
Keeps blocked transcribed uploads out of the retrieval index
Its calibration is a quality check whose failure demotes sampled autonomy

nodes.name: Compliance Knowledge & Readiness Reporting
nodes.summary: The typed catalogue of frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001 slices), requirements, controls and 14 tests (GH-1..5, HR-1..5, AWS-1..3, IDP-1), with declarative checks, the impact table, rule versions, the lookup table and the versioned fix catalogue. It rolls current compliance state up into framework readiness reports, governs how rule changes are applied to past verdicts, proposes framework mappings with a computed confidence, and lets a model draft declarative checks offline that code gates and a named reviewer promotes.

businessRules: Tier routing: a deterministic test is tier 1, one evidence type is tier 2, more is tier 3
Every catalogue cross-reference must resolve when the graph loads
A requirement takes the worst state of its tests' subjects: fail > needs_review > pending > partial > pass
Unassessed, parked, stale or incompletely inventoried subjects count as pending, never as pass
A correction that turns FAIL into PASS needs a named sign-off
A mapping proposal abstains below the minimum score; a model may only choose among code's ranked candidates and its confidence is kept beside code's, never in place of it
A drafted check is promoted only when the compile, paths, fixtures and shadow gates all pass and a named reviewer accepts; each accept is a new catalogue version
A tenant overlay of custom controls and tests may not replace a common entry (it is loaded and versioned, not yet wired into evaluations)
crossDomainInteractions: Tells the evaluators which tier, rule and evidence each test needs
Supplies lookup plans and the fix catalogue to fix suggestions
Reads the bitemporal state heads and exceptions to build reports
Supplies the rollup facts that audit-prep tasks settle from

nodes.name: Compliance Evaluation
nodes.summary: Produces verdicts for every (test, subject) pair: tier 1 deterministic and declarative rules, tier 2 extract-then-rule with verified citations, and tier 3 agentic workflows that stop at a human gate when confidence is low. Re-evaluation is triggered by entity changes, staleness clocks and full runs.

businessRules: A hashed evaluation key makes retries no-ops; a stored verdict is never recomputed
A verdict and its announcement on the verdicts topic commit in one transaction
One in-flight evaluation per subject, under a tenant concurrency cap
AI tiers park when the tenant's daily model budget is spent
A PASS or PARTIAL resting on an incomplete or stale population is withheld as needs_review
The model only extracts cited fields; a code rule decides, and every quote must be verbatim from a shown chunk
Every AI PASS is checked by a second reader from a different model
crossDomainInteractions: Publishes verdicts that become bitemporal compliance state
Fail and needs_review verdicts queue lookups (tests with a plan) or Investigator jobs
Later verdicts confirm or reopen fix suggestions
Tier 3 drafts below the confidence threshold open human approval items

nodes.name: Compliance State & Exceptions
nodes.summary: An append-only bitemporal compliance-state table that records what was true (valid time) and when it was known (transaction time) for every subject, plus the end-to-end per-tenant pipeline, findings views and time-boxed control exceptions decided through the approval stage.

businessRules: State rows are append-only and written under a per-subject advisory lock
Late facts are filed into history bounded at the next newer fact
Each row carries a reason: evaluation, human_override, correction, rule_change, stale_evidence or late_event
An exception covers one currently failing subject until an end date and is decided by a member other than the requester
Only a failure reads as 'fail (excepted until D)'
crossDomainInteractions: Consumes verdicts from the evaluation domain
Exceptions are minted inside the approving decision's transaction
Feeds readiness rollups, findings pages, agent state tools, the coverage map, questionnaire directions and as-of audit packages

nodes.name: AWS Coverage & Service Playbooks
nodes.summary: Measures coverage from what the customer's AWS account actually holds: a daily AWS Config inventory snapshot, service classes with their intents, and a coverage map that gives every resource and intent pass, fail, pending, gap or not_assessed. New resource types queue for a named person's class decision, and daily service playbooks read coverage gaps read-only, recording only fail or needs_review, never pass.

businessRules: Inventory responses land as raw evidence first; a recorder that is off gives an incomplete snapshot, never an empty whole one
A resource of an unclassified type, or in an incomplete inventory, is not_assessed
An intent with no covering deterministic test is a gap, never a pass
A class for a new resource type is approved by a named person, appended to the YAML and logged
The registry diff reads AWS's public type list with CCP's own credentials and touches no customer account
Playbooks decide known fields in code by JSON Pointer; otherwise a tool-less, fenced model reading must cite pointers and values that code verifies
A playbook records fail or needs_review only, within a daily read cap; a reading that sees nothing wrong records nothing or 'cleared'
crossDomainInteractions: Reads the deterministic verdict heads that decide covered intents
Reads AWS Config through the onboarded role and lands responses through ingestion
Its inventory, registry-diff and playbook jobs are fired by the scheduler

nodes.name: AI Compliance Agents
nodes.summary: LangGraph agents on one shared core and one read-only tool surface: the Investigator diagnoses failing verdicts the rule cannot explain, reads the lookups code made and chooses catalogue fixes by id for code to render; the Policy Agent analyzes policy gaps and drafts Markdown policy; and the Compliance Copilot answers operator questions with verified citations. Agents only read and propose; people can watch and stop any run.

businessRules: Every tool call passes the BoundTool gateway: per-graph allowlist, default-deny policy check, argument and output validation, redaction
Tools run on a read-only database role under row-level security; agents propose, never act
The Investigator writes no command or diff: it chooses a fix id and parameters, which the graph bounds to the test's catalogue fixes and their patterns (correctable once)
Evidence and tool output enter prompts only through nonce fences of the prompt guard
Tool loops end only through a stop reason (call cap, repeated call, errors, budget, refusal)
Proposed action targets are re-validated against tenant data before any proposal is written
Drafts are scrubbed of secrets and other tenants' names
crossDomainInteractions: Model-chosen fixes are rendered and offered as fix suggestions
Read stored lookups through the get_lookups tool
Agent tools read evidence through hybrid retrieval and state through the compliance-state readers
Run logs feed replay and harness metrics

nodes.name: Long Compliance Tasks
nodes.summary: Long-running audit-preparation and security-questionnaire tasks modelled as typed rows. Code planners write items, code settles what verdicts already answer, and the remainder is read by task_item agent runs (single run or fanned out) under spend and deadline caps, with people answering open questions.

businessRules: The task runner is the only code that changes task and item statuses
The forecast is expected reads times the p95 item cost; spend and deadline caps park the task
Code settles check items from verdict states before any model read
Fan-out runs only when enabled for the kind and a single-run baseline exists
Items past the per-item run limit are held for a person
A person's answer is read back as quoted, untrusted text
crossDomainInteractions: Settles audit-prep checks from the same rollup readings as reports
Item reads use the agent tool surface and document tools
Fanned-out items travel on the task_items topic
Its Facts snapshot is the verdict reading the questionnaire pipeline reuses

nodes.name: Security Questionnaires
nodes.summary: Answers customer security questionnaires through a fixed pipeline, not an agent: map each question to a tested control, reuse a still-true approved library answer, derive yes or no from current verdicts, retrieve evidence, draft with two tool-less model steps over fenced chunks and check the draft in code. A person approves and sends; answers go stale when the verdicts or documents they rested on change, and every send is attested under the publication policy.

businessRules: A control's current verdict states decide yes, no, pending or undecided; the prose must follow a decided direction
Each fact's quote must be in its chunk or the fact is dropped; every number in the prose must appear in the question or a checked fact
Without a model key a decided direction still gets a code-written answer and an undecided one says so
A library answer is reused only while nothing it rested on changed (exact question key, else at least 80% shared words)
A draft that failed a code check is approved only with the reviewer's own text
Sending is refused until every answer is approved and current and the publication policy allows the assertion
Library answers skip review only at a sampled autonomy level
crossDomainInteractions: Reads verdict states for answer direction and goes stale when they change
Retrieves policy documents and control evidence through hybrid search
Attests each send under the publication policy
Library answers pass through the autonomy decision

nodes.name: Human Approval Stage & Review Autonomy
nodes.summary: One shared, append-only approval stage gates every pause and action: tier 3 decisions, control exceptions, identity merges, scope changes, evidence requests and the opt-in GitHub remediation and rollback. Decisions are bound to the exact payload shown. Separately, autonomy levels decide which AI drafts may skip a person's review: only reversible, low-impact classes, only at a level promoted on a published quality snapshot, within a daily exposure budget and a seeded review sample.

businessRules: Only a signed-in member with the required role may decide, never the requester
A decision is accepted only for the payload hash the reviewer was shown; double decisions are refused
Items expire per kind and must be reopened after expiry
Break-glass is admin-only, for urgent kinds, needs a 20+ character reason and opens a second-approver review
Tier 3 decisions are applied exactly once from the applies topic

Sampled autonomy needs a reversible, low-impact class and a published snapshot measured on the release bundle in force that meets the bar (false-accept upper bound of at most 1% on at least 300 FAIL-labelled cases, pass^k of at least 0.90)
At sampled, drafts are auto-accepted within 50 a day per tenant and class, with a 10% seeded sample still reviewed
A bundle change or a failed relabel, adequacy, canary or judged-sample check demotes a sampled class to approve_each
crossDomainInteractions: Resumes tier 3 evaluation graphs from recorded decisions
Mints control exceptions and links or separates identities
Grants opt-in remediation execution and applies tenant scope changes
Promotes autonomy only on published quality snapshots

nodes.name: Fix Suggestions & Confirmation
nodes.summary: CCP suggests fixes and applies none. After a FAIL, code-chosen lookups read AWS Config history, CloudTrail and the organization's Terraform about each failing resource and land the responses raw first. When the rule explains the failure, code writes the investigation; otherwise the Investigator picks fixes by id. Code renders each fix from the versioned catalogue and checks it offline, a person records accept or dismiss, and only a later read confirms the fix or reopens it within 30 days. The live GitHub collaborator removal behind five gates remains, opt-in and off by default.

entities: Offline check (params, cli, syntax, scope, placeholders)
Suggestion event (open, accepted, dismissed, confirmed, reopened, superseded)
businessRules: Code chooses every read from the verdict and the lookup table; a model never chooses a live read or its parameters
Lookup responses land as raw evidence first; a read with no live connection is recorded as skipped and a refused call as error
A model writes no command or diff: it picks a fix id and parameters, and code renders by filling placeholders only, with shell-quoted values
A rendering is offered only when the params, cli, syntax, scope and placeholder checks all pass
One live suggestion exists per test, resource and fix; an identical payload returns the existing one
Accept and dismiss never confirm: only a later verdict whose evidence was observed after the suggestion confirms it, and a failure within 30 days reopens it
Live GitHub removal needs CCP_REMEDIATION_LIVE (off by default), --live, an allowlisted repo and unprotected login, a typed confirmation and an approval matching the payload hash
crossDomainInteractions: Triggered by fail and needs_review verdicts and settled by later ones
Lands lookup responses through ingestion's raw landing
Feeds the Investigator through the get_lookups tool
Opt-in proposals open approval items and spend execution grants
Method cards explain how each suggestion was chosen and rendered

nodes.name: Tenants, Cells, Membership & Sign-in
nodes.summary: Tenants are data: onboarded without a deploy, with append-only versioned settings and role-based memberships. Members sign in through a local dev issuer or OIDC with PKCE, and every request is resolved to a tenant, principal and role. Each tenant lives in one deployment cell that fixes its region, data residency and model route, behind a transaction pooler, a lag-bounded read replica and, for the largest tenants, partitions of their own.

businessRules: All tenant data is read through ScopedDB so row-level security applies
Free settings fields are recorded directly; rule-affecting or connection changes need an approved scope_change against the current version
A non-member gets the same 404 as an unknown tenant
The last admin of a tenant cannot be removed or demoted
Tokens must be RS256/ES256 and verified against published JWKS
UI sessions use HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookies and per-session CSRF tokens
A process serves only its own cell's tenants; an EU cell reaches models through regional Bedrock profiles with CCP's pinned ids mapped at the SDK boundary
Lag-tolerant reads go to the replica only while its replay lag is within the bound, else the primary
Only allowlisted tables outside the audit chain whose unique keys start with tenant_id may be partitioned by tenant
crossDomainInteractions: Scope changes and decisions are routed through the approval stage
Tenant settings parameterize evaluator rules and connections
The cell decides which provider every model call and embedding reaches

nodes.name: Model Quality & Eval Harness
nodes.summary: Measures every model-backed step: golden and adversarial eval suites with exact grading and an LLM judge, judge calibration against human labels, regression gates on release bundles, production canaries, nightly judged samples and monthly expert relabels, agent harness gates, and quarterly published quality snapshots per AI workflow.

businessRules: The judge never grades output its own model produced, and a non-Anthropic judge never sees customer-derived cases
Content-free outputs fail in code before reaching the judge
A judged case passes only when repeated runs and bias variants agree
A deterministic pass-to-fail flip fails the regression gate
AI tests are gated on pass^k floors and false-PASS ceilings with Wilson intervals
Reviewer labels holding customer data are never written inside the repository
A candidate bundle with more loop or cap stops than the baseline is blocked
A published false-PASS bound resting on fewer FAIL-labelled cases than the minimum is withheld and the count shown instead
crossDomainInteractions: Runs evaluator, agent, retrieval and pipeline targets as eval cases
Samples production AI verdicts for judging
Tunes the human-interrupt confidence threshold
Publishes the snapshots that set the bar for sampled autonomy and appear on method cards

nodes.name: Audit Integrity & Replay
nodes.summary: Lets an auditor trust the records: a per-tenant tamper-evident hash chain with signed, write-once checkpoints, re-hashing of raw-zone objects, replay of any stored model request, and a nightly sentinel that re-derives tier-1 verdicts from what they read.

businessRules: Triggers chain the record tables into a per-tenant hash chain
Checkpoints are signed over canonical JSON and exported write-once (S3 Object Lock compliance mode)
Verification re-hashes every chained row and checks every checkpoint signature
A replay rebuilds the exact prompt, schema and fenced evidence and diffs it against what was sent
A tier-1 verdict must re-derive exactly from its recorded manifest, or be explained by a rule change
crossDomainInteractions: Re-derives evaluation verdicts and replays agent and evaluator model calls
Re-hashes raw-zone objects landed by ingestion
Checkpoint and verify jobs are fired by the scheduler
Signs the checkpoint every audit package is proven under

nodes.name: Audit Packages & Auditor Assurance
nodes.summary: What CCP asserts outside itself: as-of audit packages for a framework (results with their method, raw evidence pointers and chain proofs under a signed checkpoint, sealed write-once) that an auditor verifies offline with a standalone script; a time-boxed, read-only auditor workspace over named packages; an attestation record of every outbound assertion under the versioned publication policy; and method cards that explain from recorded facts how a verdict or fix suggestion was decided.

businessRules: A package reads each subject's state true at valid_at as recorded by known_at (the bitemporal read)
A correction package carries only the subjects whose verdict changed since the package it corrects
The offline verifier needs only the standard library and cryptography, and says so when no public key is pinned
A grant lasts 1 to 90 days and is judged under the publication policy first; a blocked share makes no grant
An expired or revoked grant answers 404, like a tenant that does not exist, and every file read is logged
Every outbound assertion records an attestation (policy version, reasons, digest of what was asserted) before anything leaves
A method card is built from recorded facts; model prose is never the card
crossDomainInteractions: Reads compliance state as of valid and known times
Proves results with audit-chain segments under a signed checkpoint
Points to raw-zone evidence with stored digests and versions
Attaches published quality snapshots to model verdicts' method cards

nodes.name: Ingest Connector Evidence
nodes.summary: Pulls every requested connector for a tenant as recorded sync runs, landing each provider event once in the immutable raw zone and appending new ones to the event log.

domainMeta.entryPoint: ccp ingest run (also the scheduled sync job)

nodes.name: Pull every requested connector
nodes.summary: Pulls each requested connector for the tenant, each as its own sync run under its declared connection.

nodes.name: Build the connector
nodes.summary: Chooses the GitHub, HRIS, manual upload, AWS or Okta connector (fixture or live) by name and source.

nodes.name: Run the pull as a sync run
nodes.summary: Runs one connector pull, lands events and responses, records each scope's outcome and turns pull errors into a failed run with an error kind.

nodes.name: Page the provider API
nodes.summary: Reads org, members, repos, collaborators and repo settings, retrying and waiting by the per-endpoint error table and reporting not-visible reads as gaps.

nodes.name: Land events with dedup
nodes.summary: Writes the raw zone first, inserts raw_events with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and appends new events to the event log; a repeated earlier state lands again as a re-observation once its stream has moved on.

nodes.name: Write once to the raw zone
nodes.summary: Stores each event once under tenant/connector/date, diverting repeats under dups/ and keeping responses content-addressed.

nodes.name: Append to the event log
nodes.summary: Appends the record to its raw.<connector> topic with a per-tenant sequence and notifies the topic's workers on commit.

nodes.name: Record the sync run
nodes.summary: Inserts the sync run and one row per scope outcome in a single transaction for completeness checks.

nodes.name: Check Connection Health
nodes.summary: Syncs declared connections into versioned rows, probes each enabled connection's credential and derives its health from checks and sync runs.

domainMeta.entryPoint: ccp connections check / ccp connections list (daily connection-check job)

nodes.name: Run the daily check
nodes.summary: Daily job that syncs connections from configuration and then probes every enabled one.

nodes.name: Sync declared connections
nodes.summary: Appends versions for new or changed connections and disables those no longer declared.

nodes.name: Probe the credential
nodes.summary: Probes one connection's credential; fixture and upload connectors are ok once buildable.

nodes.name: Record the check outcome
nodes.summary: Appends a connection_checks row with the probe outcome and detail.

nodes.name: Derive connection health
nodes.summary: Pure derivation of health from the newest check, the latest run's status, error kind and finish time.

nodes.name: Report health per connection
nodes.summary: Computes the health of every current connection from stored checks and sync runs for display.

nodes.name: Onboard an AWS Account
nodes.summary: Generates a per-account external ID and quick-create link for the read-only CCPReadOnly role, verifies the role before anything is read, and wires it into the AWS connection.

domainMeta.entryPoint: ccp aws onboard / ccp aws verify

nodes.name: Validate the account ID
nodes.summary: Requires an AWS account ID of exactly 12 digits.

nodes.name: Start onboarding with an external ID
nodes.summary: Records a new unguessable external ID pending verification, or reuses the one already started.

nodes.name: Build the quick-create link
nodes.summary: Builds the CloudFormation console link for the CCPReadOnly stack with the template URL and external ID.

nodes.name: Verify the read-only role
nodes.summary: Checks the role is assumable with the external ID, refused without it, and can neither write nor escalate.

nodes.name: Record the verification
nodes.summary: Appends a verified or refused onboarding version, refusing accounts never started.

nodes.name: Attach the role to the connection
nodes.summary: Gives the AWS connection the verified role ARN and external ID; unverified accounts get none.

nodes.name: Pull AWS snapshots
nodes.summary: Assumes the customer role via STS and lands content-addressed snapshots of the account, S3 buckets and IAM users.

nodes.name: Transcribe Scanned Uploads
nodes.summary: Transcribes scanned PDF pages and screenshot uploads with Claude vision and lands the text as derived manual.transcribed events.

domainMeta.entryPoint: ccp ingest transcribe (also the scheduled transcription job)

nodes.name: Find pending uploads
nodes.summary: Returns upload events that carry an attachment and have no transcription yet.

nodes.name: Read digest-checked bytes
nodes.summary: Reads the attachment from the raw zone only when its bytes match the digest the event names.

nodes.name: Split blank pages
nodes.summary: Produces one single-page PDF per page with no text layer, in the same capped child process.

nodes.name: Transcribe each page
nodes.summary: Sends one page or image to the model with the transcription prompt as a structured extraction.

nodes.name: Build the derived event
nodes.summary: Builds the manual.transcribed SourceEvent from the upload event and its page transcriptions.

nodes.name: Record and land transcriptions
nodes.summary: Runs within page and time budgets, records transcriptions and lands the derived events.

nodes.name: Run Connector Conformance
nodes.summary: Runs every live connector's recorded scenarios offline through real code, plus sabotaged negative controls, proving the connector contract promises hold.

domainMeta.entryPoint: ccp connectors conformance

nodes.name: Load suites and controls
nodes.summary: Loads the GitHub and upload-folder conformance suites and their negative controls.

nodes.name: Serve the recorded API
nodes.summary: Serves a fixed recorded GitHub world with per-path scenario overrides as an HTTP transport.

nodes.name: Pull one scenario
nodes.summary: Runs a scenario's pull capturing events, the SyncReport, the stop kind and requested sleeps.

nodes.name: Check contract promises
nodes.summary: Checks a pull against every promise, including a second pull for repeatable snapshot ids.

nodes.name: Check recordings hold no secrets
nodes.summary: Scans recording text for tokens, AWS key ids, authorization headers and private keys.

nodes.name: Run negative controls
nodes.summary: Runs sabotaged connectors (hidden read as empty, complete over gaps, ids from pull time) that must fail.

nodes.name: Report blind spots
nodes.summary: Aggregates results; green only when every scenario passes and every negative control is caught.

nodes.name: Dispatch Consumer Work Across Tenants
nodes.summary: Runs a registered event-log consumer over many tenants fairly: wakes on notifications or due hints, claims the tenant served longest ago, processes leased records and settles each outcome.

domainMeta.entryPoint: ccp worker run

nodes.name: Start the dispatcher
nodes.summary: Builds a Dispatcher for one registered consumer and its tenants and runs it once or continuously.

nodes.name: Mark tenants ready
nodes.summary: Upserts work hints so a notification is never lost, overriding held or idle hints.

nodes.name: Claim the longest-waiting tenant
nodes.summary: Claims the ready hint served longest ago through a SKIP LOCKED pick and holds it.

nodes.name: Claim due records under leases
nodes.summary: Claims due records as fresh leases, optionally at most one per partition key.

nodes.name: Process records within the cap
nodes.summary: Handles leased records within the tenant's in-flight cap; ordered topics use OrderedConsumer instead.

nodes.name: Renew held leases
nodes.summary: A daemon thread renews held leases every third of the lease length and tracks lost leases.

nodes.name: Retry, defer, park or dead-letter
nodes.summary: Returns a failed record to pending after jittered backoff; throttled records defer, budget stops park, terminal errors dead-letter.

nodes.name: Release the work hint
nodes.summary: Puts the hint back with its next ready time unless a notification re-marked it meanwhile.

nodes.name: Fire Scheduled Jobs
nodes.summary: Syncs each tenant's configured schedules, fires every due slot exactly once across processes and dispatches it to a named job such as the clock tick, full run, connection check, sentinel or audit checkpoint.

domainMeta.entryPoint: Scheduler worker pass (per-tenant wall-clock schedules)

nodes.name: Run a scheduler pass
nodes.summary: Worker-loop adapter that syncs configuration and fires due slots, reporting the next due time.

nodes.name: Sync tenant schedules
nodes.summary: Upserts configured schedules, recomputing next slots for new or changed ones and disabling removed ones.

nodes.name: Compute the next slot
nodes.summary: Computes the next UTC moment for 'every N minutes/hours' or 'daily HH:MM' in the tenant time zone, resolving DST gaps.

nodes.name: Fire each due slot once
nodes.summary: Under SKIP LOCKED, counts missed slots, appends one jobs record and inserts the schedule_runs row.

nodes.name: Hold dependent tests

nodes.name: Build the reviewer card

nodes.name: Decide merge or distinct
nodes.summary: Lists open reviews or resolves one as merge or distinct through a signed-in approver's approval action.

nodes.name: Write the resolution
nodes.summary: Inside the deciding event's transaction, records the resolution and links persons or keeps them apart.

nodes.name: Refresh the Retrieval Index

nodes.name: Refresh over current evidence
nodes.summary: Walks every current evidence row, drops inadmissible ones, records new chunk sets or tombstones and updates serving chunks when active.

nodes.summary: Leaves out an uploaded, model-transcribed document with a blocking admissibility reason; everything else counts.

nodes.name: Decide the target generation
nodes.summary: Decides whether the embedder's generation serves: 'first' for a new tenant, 'forced' on rebuild, otherwise a candidate.

nodes.name: Chunk evidence page by page

nodes.name: Embed through the cache

nodes.name: Record the chunk set

nodes.name: Project serving chunks
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the serving chunks table from the generation's newest set of every current evidence entity.

nodes.name: Hybrid Evidence Search

nodes.name: Check the embedding model
nodes.summary: Refuses retrieval when serving chunks were embedded with another model than the query embedder.

nodes.name: Build the text query

nodes.name: Fuse lexical and vector arms

nodes.name: Rerank candidates

nodes.name: Score retrieval confidence

nodes.name: Ensure the generation

nodes.name: Refresh into the candidate

nodes.name: Measure on golden queries
nodes.summary: Scores Recall@5, MRR and nDCG@10 for every golden query against resolved relevant chunks.

nodes.name: Gate the candidate
nodes.summary: Passes only if the candidate resolves queries and loses no more than the tolerance on Recall@5 or MRR.

nodes.name: Activate the generation
nodes.summary: Records an insert-only, chained activation with its reason and gate result.

nodes.name: Calibrate Retrieval and Check Gates

nodes.name: Save the retrieval config
nodes.summary: Writes thresholds and curves back to config/retrieval.yaml.

nodes.name: List blocking reasons
nodes.summary: Lists every per-type breach and unresolved golden query that blocks the report.

nodes.name: Bound false accepts

nodes.name: Gate showing answers
nodes.summary: Reports whether the newest adequacy calibration check passed, which lets live mode show answers.

nodes.name: Read the latest snapshots

nodes.name: Read verdict heads

nodes.name: Read the latest inventory

nodes.name: Summarize coverage

nodes.name: Offer the fix suggestions

nodes.name: Run gap or draft mode

nodes.name: Analyze requirement coverage

nodes.name: Scrub the draft text

nodes.name: Start the session

nodes.name: Run one turn

nodes.name: Stream the answer text

nodes.summary: Inserts one CopilotAnswer row with citations, requested actions and guardrail events.

nodes.name: Describe the requested action
nodes.summary: Describes exactly what a confirmation would open, with target, reversibility and the verdict it fixes.

nodes.name: Decide by policy

nodes.name: Run through the gateway
nodes.summary: Enforces call limits, pinned args, validation, taint rule, timeout and redaction around execution.

nodes.name: Map the result to HTTP
nodes.summary: Maps the gateway result to 200, 403 for policy denials, 429 for limits or 500 for malformed results.

nodes.summary: Inserts a run_stops row, returning False when one was already made.

nodes.name: Poll for the stop

nodes.name: Raise RunStopped

nodes.name: Mark the thread cancelled
nodes.summary: Marks the thread cancelled, keeping its record and trajectory.

nodes.summary: Builds an audit_prep or questionnaire scope from options or a YAML file.

nodes.name: Plan audit-prep items
nodes.summary: Writes one check item per in-scope test, settled later from verdict states.

nodes.name: Plan with forecast and caps
nodes.summary: Forecasts expected reads times item cost and sets default caps.

nodes.name: Create task rows

nodes.name: Advance open tasks
nodes.summary: Scheduled job that advances every open task once per slot.

nodes.name: Run one task pass
nodes.summary: Applies the deadline cap, settles checks, adds follow-ups and rechecks reads before the reader.

nodes.name: Snapshot the facts
nodes.summary: Per-pass snapshot of state heads, the knowledge graph and rollup coverage.

nodes.name: Choose the reader

nodes.name: Run the task_item graph

nodes.name: Check readings in code

nodes.name: Merge the item reading

nodes.name: Park on a cap
nodes.summary: Parks the task with a reason when budget or repeated stalls stop it.

nodes.name: Merge the reading

nodes.name: Drain item jobs

nodes.name: Build the item payload
nodes.summary: Builds typed inputs with the newest human answer and no earlier model output.

nodes.name: Merge the new reading
nodes.summary: Applies code checks to the new reading and writes the item's status.

nodes.name: Answer each question

nodes.name: Approve a draft

nodes.name: Reject a draft
nodes.summary: Rejects a drafted answer with a mandatory note.

nodes.name: Send the questionnaire

nodes.name: Record the attestation

nodes.name: Explain what changed

nodes.name: Record the stale event

nodes.name: Compute questionnaire metrics

nodes.summary: The only constructor: validates action, reviewer and any override status.

nodes.summary: Parallel consumer applying each recorded decision once.

nodes.summary: Continues only from a decision recorded on the approval item whose payload hash matches the interrupt.
